The affidavit of the Collector, Rewa and its contents as mentioned in paragraph 10, when read in conjunction with submissions made by her in paragraph 6 to 9 which are reproduced herein for better understanding of the facts reveals that prima facie Collector, Rewa has not appreciated law in the correct perspective:
"6.
That, the petitioner came to the note the proceeding of Land Acquisition Officer has been initiated under the provision of Section 4A and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The petitioner submitted that in the Notification under Section 4 which was issued on 23.12.2005, was without disclosing the full purpose of acquisition.
It is further submitted that the petitioner was trying to submit the objection under Section 5A of the Act but the authorities has declined to accept the same.

However,
the petitioner has send the objection through registered post.

On an 2 WP-11539-2007 application under Section 6(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, on 07.06.2007, the petitioner has got the information that the land has been acquired for the purpose of construction of hostel for MBA Department of the University.
It is further submitted that henceforth, the petitioner has filed the objection before the respondent No.3 and further reminded on 22.06.2007, but no action has been taken.

7. final award has been passed by the Land Acquisition Officer vide award dated 21.05.2008 and valuation of the land of the petitioner, has been valued at Rs.32,36,450/-.
8.
That, it is further respectfully submitted by the deponent that the respondent-University had submitted 13,50,000/- through cheque no. 013112 dated 25 June 2003.

Land Acquisition Officer,
wrote a letter to the University, for depositing of the remaining amount of compensation, in view of the award dated 21.05.2008.

However, vide communication dated 15.05.2009, again the request has been made to the respondent-University for deposited the amount of compensation so that the amount may be disbursed to the land owners.

9. It is further submitted by the deponent before this Hon'ble Court that the respondent-University had filed a reference under 3 WP-11539-2007 Section 18 of the Act of 1894, before the Reference Court, against the award dated 21.05.2008 where the respondent- University had made a dispute regarding the computation of compensation before the Reference Court.
The remaining amount was not deposited by the respondent-University till 2015.Vide order dated 08.10.2015, the Reference Court had rejected, the reference preferred by the respondent-University.

Through Cheque no.
055150 dated 24 May 2016, respondent-University submitted the remaining amount of 97,44,611/-
10.
The then collector has further passed an award on 21.03.2017 by granting the benefit of the interest in terms of Section 30 of the Act of 2013.
Therefore, in addition to the original award of 1,10,94,611/-, additional interest of 1,48,61,104/- was declared by the collector vide order dated 21.03.2017.
The additional interest amount was submitted by the respondent-University through cheque no. 062415 dated 17.11.2017."
Section 30 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (the Act of 2013) deals with award of solatium.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: How, Collector is authorised to award solatium on 21.03.2017 when she had already become functus officio after original award was passed on 21.05.2008 and thereafter admittedly Awadhesh Pratap Singh University, Rewa did not deposit the amount determined by the Land Acquisition Officer, as is noted by Collector, Rewa then in terms of Section 24 of the Act of 2013, proceedings shall be deemed 4 WP-11539-2007 to have been lapsed.
Thus, it is not evident that how Collector was entitled to pass another award as mentioned in paragraph 10 of the affidavit on 21.03.2017 and wherefrom she drew that authority.
Let a further affidavit be filed by Collector Rewa duly vetted by the Advocate General of the State within ten days from today.

In the meanwhile, Registrar of the University will also file an affidavit in the light of Section 24 of the Act of 2013 because Shri Bilaiya admits that the amount of compensation was not deposited till 08.10.2015 even when the reference was rejected and some amount was deposited on 24th May,
2016 and hence, whether that will protect the University from the rigours of Section 24 of the Act of 2013, is to be brought on record.

Let necessary facts be brought on record duly vetted by the Counsel for the University first because that will have legal sanction otherwise anything written by officers of the University or District Administration without being vetted by the respective competent law Yadu Nandan Shukla(Dead) Through Legal ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163178020/
